subject.title: fix(agents): reject malformed bundle LSP frames when content length is invalid

question: Should bundle LSP startup deliberately stop supporting servers that emit duplicate or non-decimal Content-Length headers, once the branch is refreshed against current main?
rationale: The stricter parser is technically sound and prevents frame desynchronization, but it intentionally converts previously tolerated protocol violations into an upgrade-visible startup failure for affected bundles.

options.title: Accept strict framing
options.body: Rebase, rerun exact-head proof, and land the fail-closed parser because malformed LSP framing should not materialize agent tools.

options.title: Require compatibility evidence
options.body: Pause landing until known bundle LSP implementations are sampled or a specific shipped compatibility contract for malformed headers is identified.

recommendation.title: Accept strict framing
recommendation.body: Rebase, rerun exact-head proof, and land the fail-closed parser because malformed LSP framing should not materialize agent tools.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work at the same bundled LSP process lifecycle boundary makes this account the clearest available reviewer for the compatibility choice.
